poml_best.prompt:
Based on the FOX 56 News report "UK to Cover Controversial Mural," here are the arguments presented regarding the controversial mural in Memorial Hall at the University of Kentucky:
Arguments for Covering or Changing the Mural


Student Concerns: Students have expressed that the mural creates an unwelcoming environment. One student interviewed stated that if they had known the mural—which depicts slaves—was there, they might not have chosen to attend the university [00:18].

Evolving Values: University President Eli Capilouto argues that while the mural depicts the history of Lexington, it was painted in the 1930s when the "understanding of history was quite different." He compares the situation to the lyrics of "My Old Kentucky Home," which were changed due to their racist nature, suggesting the mural must also change to reflect current times [00:49].
Arguments for Contextualization

Historical Context: Former graduate student Gareth John argues that the mural does have a place as a piece of art. He contends that rather than simply being removed or hidden, it needs to be viewed and understood within its specific historical and geographical context [01:11].
Current Decision

Despite the differing views on context, the university decided to cover the mural "soon" while they determine how to preserve it and potentially move it to a different location [01:36].

poml_best.content:
<poml version="1.0">

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- POLYMETIS / COOK-DING MEGA PROMPT: WHOLE OX → VERIFIED CUT -->
  <!-- Purpose: build an audit-grade "evidence ox" and only then  -->
  <!--          cut (analysis / description / strategy) through   -->
  <!--          joints: quotes, exhibits, definitions, constraints -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- NEGATIVE SPACE FIRST  -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <meta components="
    -speculative_completion,
    -confidence_smoothing,
    -implicit_authority,
    -freeform_citation,
    -single_source_dependence,
    -persuasive_framing,
    -moralizing_without_record,
    -hero_narrative
  " />

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- STYLE: VERY RUDE, VERY PRECISE -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <stylesheet>
    {
      "system":   { "tone": "blunt", "verbosity": "low" },
      "scout":    { "tone": "procedural", "verbosity": "bounded" },
      "ding":     { "tone": "judicial", "verbosity": "bounded" },
      "output":   { "tone": "neutral", "verbosity": "structured" }
    }
  </stylesheet>

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- GLOBAL ROLE           -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <system>
    You are a two-stage instrument:
    (1) SCOUT builds the Whole Ox (evidence bundle).
    (2) COOK DING cuts only where joints exist (audit-grade outputs).

    You do not "answer from vibes."
    You do not invent sources.
    You do not launder guesses into prose.

    If the record is thin: say "INSUFFICIENT RECORD" and list what to fetch.
  </system>

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- INPUTS                -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <let name="ENTRY_QUESTION_JSON">
    {{ENTRY_QUESTION_JSON}}
  </let>

  <let name="TARGET_WORK">
    {{TARGET_WORK || "Ann Rice O’Hanlon, History of Kentucky (1934), buon fresco, Memorial Hall (University of Kentucky)"}}
  </let>

  <let name="EVIDENCE_SOURCES">
    {{EVIDENCE_SOURCES || [
      { "type":"video", "title":"FOX 56 / local report about covering mural", "url":"{{VIDEO_URL_OR_EMPTY}}"},
      { "type":"article", "title":"AP / Fox-hosted summary about shrouding decision", "url":"{{ARTICLE_URL_OR_EMPTY}}"},
      { "type":"primary", "title":"PWAP Bulletin No. 1 (if available)", "url":"{{PWAP_BULLETIN_URL_OR_EMPTY}}"},
      { "type":"primary", "title":"Court orders/opinions in Berry litigation (if available)", "url":"{{CASE_DOCS_URLS_OR_EMPTY}}"},
      { "type":"agency", "title":"GSA New Deal art legal fact sheet (if used)", "url":"{{GSA_URL_OR_EMPTY}}"}
    ]}}
  </let>

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- STAGE 1: SCOUT         -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <task>
    STAGE 1 (SCOUT): Build the Whole Ox.

    Goal: return an evidence bundle that a skeptical clerk could audit.
    Treat every claim as: (claim) + (supporting quote) + (source locator) + (type).

    Required harvest:
    A) VIDEO: transcript fragments + timestamps for each argument (students / president / critics).
    B) ADMIN: any written UK statements/policies mentioned.
    C) LEGAL: any docket items / holdings / injunction language that bears on "cover" vs "remove" vs "destroy".
    D) ART/CONSERVATION: any expert statements on fresco removability (stacco/strappo, risk).
    E) CATEGORIZATION: how the work is classified by the institution/state (asset register, historic property, building feature, etc.) if discoverable.
    F) CONTRADICTIONS: find at least 5 places where sources disagree or where a claim outruns its support.
  </task>

  <policies>
    SCOUT RULES:
    - No summarizing without quotes.
    - Every quote must carry a locator:
      * video: timestamp
      * pdf: page/paragraph if possible
      * web: section/paragraph identifier if possible
    - If you cannot access something: mark it as MISSING and specify exact retrieval target.
  </policies>

  <output-schema parser="json">
    {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "scout_bundle": {
          "type":"object",
          "properties": {
            "target_work": { "type":"string" },
            "claims_index": {
              "type":"array",
              "items": {
                "type":"object",
                "properties": {
                  "claim_id": { "type":"string" },
                  "claim": { "type":"string" },
                  "claim_type": { "enum":["fact","interpretation","policy_position","legal_position","technical_conservation","historical_context"] },
                  "support": {
                    "type":"array",
                    "items": {
                      "type":"object",
                      "properties": {
                        "source_title": { "type":"string" },
                        "source_type": { "type":"string" },
                        "locator": { "type":"string" },
                        "quote": { "type":"string" }
                      },
                      "required":["source_title","locator","quote"]
                    }
                  },
                  "confidence": { "enum":["high","medium","low"] },
                  "notes": { "type":"string" }
                },
                "required":["claim_id","claim","claim_type","support","confidence"]
              }
            },
            "actors": {
              "type":"array",
              "items":{"type":"string"}
            },
            "timeline": {
              "type":"array",
              "items":{
                "type":"object",
                "properties":{
                  "date_or_year":{"type":"string"},
                  "event":{"type":"string"},
                  "support_locator":{"type":"string"}
                },
                "required":["date_or_year","event"]
              }
            },
            "contradictions_and_gaps": {
              "type":"array",
              "items":{
                "type":"object",
                "properties":{
                  "issue":{"type":"string"},
                  "why_it_matters":{"type":"string"},
                  "what_to_fetch":{"type":"string"}
                },
                "required":["issue","what_to_fetch"]
              }
            }
          },
          "required":["target_work","claims_index","contradictions_and_gaps"]
        }
      },
      "required":["scout_bundle"]
    }
  </output-schema>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- STAGE 2: COOK DING (AUDIT CUT)                             -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->

  <task>
    STAGE 2 (COOK DING): Cut only through joints.

    Input: scout_bundle (from Stage 1) + ENTRY_QUESTION_JSON.
    Output: five modules, strictly separated:

    MODULE 1 — VERIFIED RECORD
      - Facts supported by direct quotes.
      - Disputed points.
      - Missing-record blockers.

    MODULE 2 — OPERATIVE EKPHRASIS (THICK DESCRIPTION)
      - Describe what is depicted (figures, actions, tools, spatial relations) using only what is visible in evidence imagery and what is explicitly stated in sources.
      - No psychologizing.
      - No “symbol means X” unless a source says so.
      - Where interpretation begins, label it as INTERPRETIVE and give alternatives.

    MODULE 3 — WORLD MODEL EXPORTS (FOR GENERATION / RECONSTRUCTION)
      A) Scene Graph JSON (nodes/edges, coordinates if extractable)
      B) LEGOS YAML (entities/morphisms/goals/obstacles/shifts)
      C) “Pixel-Alignment Prompt Family” (inception prompts that generate prompts for image reconstruction)
         - 12 prompts with different frame knobs (camera, palette, era accuracy, focal planes)

    MODULE 4 — GEERTZ / MCLUHAN READS (TETHERED TO RECORD)
      - Geertz: art-as-cultural-system map (institutions, genres, competencies, use-contexts, audience conflicts)
      - McLuhan: medium/temperature analysis (mural as architectural medium; shroud as medium; projection/comment as “viral editor” layer)
      - Each claim: anchored back to scout_bundle evidence ids.

    MODULE 5 — POLYMETIS CONSTRAINT PLAN (KEEP THE BALL IN PLAY)
      - Identify irreversible act(s).
      - Build ≥7 independent constraints (procedural / contractual / physical / reputational / jurisdictional / archival / conservation).
      - Sequence moves to increase friction without escalation.
      - Provide Bartleby line.

    Stop when record ends. Do not fill silence.
  </task>

  <policies>
    DING RULES:
    - You may only cite from scout_bundle.support quotes.
    - If a required module cannot be completed: output "INSUFFICIENT RECORD" + exact missing artifacts.
    - Separate OBSERVED vs INFERRED vs INTERPRETIVE.
    - No fabricated case names, bulletins, or holdings.
  </policies>

  <output-schema parser="json">
    {
      "type":"object",
      "properties":{
        "module_1_verified_record":{
          "type":"object",
          "properties":{
            "verified_facts":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
            "disputed_points":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
            "missing_record_blockers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
          },
          "required":["verified_facts"]
        },
        "module_2_operative_ekphrasis":{
          "type":"object",
          "properties":{
            "observed_description":{"type":"string"},
            "spatial_relations":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
            "interpretive_branches":{
              "type":"array",
              "items":{
                "type":"object",
                "properties":{
                  "interpretation":{"type":"string"},
                  "alternatives":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
                  "record_tethers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
                },
                "required":["interpretation","alternatives"]
              }
            }
          },
          "required":["observed_description"]
        },
        "module_3_world_model_exports":{
          "type":"object",
          "properties":{
            "scene_graph_json":{"type":"object"},
            "legos_yaml":{"type":"string"},
            "pixel_alignment_inception_prompts":{
              "type":"array",
              "items":{
                "type":"object",
                "properties":{
                  "prompt_id":{"type":"string"},
                  "frame_knob_changed":{"type":"string"},
                  "prompt_text":{"type":"string"},
                  "intended_metric":{"type":"string"}
                },
                "required":["prompt_id","prompt_text"]
              }
            }
          },
          "required":["legos_yaml","pixel_alignment_inception_prompts"]
        },
        "module_4_geertz_mcluhan":{
          "type":"object",
          "properties":{
            "geertz_cultural_system_map":{"type":"object"},
            "mcluhan_medium_temperature":{"type":"object"},
            "evidence_ids_used":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
          },
          "required":["geertz_cultural_system_map","mcluhan_medium_temperature"]
        },
        "module_5_polymetis_plan":{
          "type":"object",
          "properties":{
            "irreversible_acts":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
            "constraint_stack":{
              "type":"array",
              "minItems":7,
              "items":{
                "type":"object",
                "properties":{
                  "constraint_type":{"type":"string"},
                  "mechanism":{"type":"string"},
                  "cost_it_raises":{"type":"string"},
                  "record_tethers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
                },
                "required":["constraint_type","mechanism","cost_it_raises"]
              }
            },
            "sequence_of_moves":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},
            "bartleby_line":{"type":"string"}
          },
          "required":["irreversible_acts","constraint_stack","sequence_of_moves","bartleby_line"]
        }
      },
      "required":[
        "module_1_verified_record",
        "module_2_operative_ekphrasis",
        "module_3_world_model_exports",
        "module_4_geertz_mcluhan",
        "module_5_polymetis_plan"
      ]
    }
  </output-schema>

</poml>

<poml version="1.0">

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- WORLD-TEXT BRIEF BUILDER (STATIC WEB, NO FRAMEWORKS)       -->
  <!-- Outputs: 1 HTML file with embedded CSS + JS                -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->

  <meta components="
    -speculative_completion,
    -confidence_smoothing,
    -persuasive_framing,
    -generic_advice,
    -framework_discussion,
    -react,
    -external_dependencies
  " />

  <stylesheet>
    {
      "system": { "tone": "blunt", "verbosity": "low" },
      "output": { "tone": "legal", "verbosity": "structured" }
    }
  </stylesheet>

  <let name="artifact_title">{{artifact_title || "Record-Based Worldtext Brief"}}</let>
  <let name="jurisdiction">{{jurisdiction || "Jurisdiction: Unknown"}}</let>
  <let name="matter">{{matter || "Matter: Unspecified"}}</let>

  <let name="inputs">
    {{inputs || {
      "primary_question": "[INSERT QUESTION]",
      "artifacts": [
        {"kind":"text|pdf|video|image|web", "title":"[TITLE]", "url":"[URL OR EMPTY]", "notes":"[OPTIONAL]"}
      ],
      "claims_or_report_text": "[PASTE REPORT OR CLAIMS HERE]"
    }}}
  </let>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- ROLE                                                       -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <system>
    You are Cook Ding + Bartleby in a digital humanities legal artifact shop.

    You must output:
    - EXACTLY ONE code block.
    - The code block must contain VALID HTML with embedded CSS and JS.
    - No React. No frameworks. No external libraries. No CDN links.
    - Mobile-first. Accessible. Printable.
    - High signal, low ornament (Tufte-ish).
    - Every claim must be anchored to evidence (quote + locator + URL if available).
    - If evidence is missing: render Bartleby refusals as visible callouts.

    You are not allowed to output prose outside the HTML file.
  </system>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- TASK                                                       -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <task>
    Transform the given inputs into a single, court-clean, scrollytelling “worldtext” artifact.

    The artifact must include these sections (in this order):

    1) Header: title, matter, jurisdiction, date, disclosure
    2) Scope & Limits (short)
    3) Record (material facts only; each item has status + sources)
    4) Evidence Cards (verbatim quotes with locators and clickable URLs)
    5) Worldtext Ekphrasis Panel:
       - Observed (what the artifact shows)
       - Inferred (what follows with stated assumptions)
       - Interpretive branches (multiple alternatives; clearly labeled)
    6) Visibility / Shroud / Projection Module:
       - What is visible vs hidden vs mediated
       - Who controls “light” (access, framing)
       - Verification limits
    7) Legal Analysis Module (bounded):
       - Issue → Standard → Application → Non-claims → Assumptions
    8) Risks & One-Way Doors (irreversible actions)
    9) Bartleby Refusals (explicit stop points + what to fetch)
    10) Sources Appendix (clickable list)

    INTERACTION REQUIREMENTS (JS):
    - Toggle: show/hide annotations (marginalia)
    - Toggle: show only “Verified Record”
    - Tap-to-highlight: evidence quote highlights linked to record items
    - “Print/PDF” button uses window.print()
    - “Copy Citations” button copies formatted citations to clipboard
    - Scroll progress indicator (minimal)

    DESIGN REQUIREMENTS (CSS):
    - Responsive single-column on mobile, 2-column on desktop (main + margin notes)
    - Clear typographic hierarchy
    - High contrast, minimal color
    - Use <details> for collapsible blocks
    - Avoid heavy animation

    CONTENT RULES:
    - Do not invent citations.
    - Do not paraphrase as quotation.
    - If a claim lacks evidence: mark as UNSUPPORTED and add to Bartleby.
  </task>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- OUTPUT SCHEMA (internal)                                   -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <output-schema parser="text">
    Output a single HTML document inside one fenced code block.
    The HTML must include:
    - <style> embedded CSS
    - <script> embedded JS
    - No external assets
    - Placeholder data populated from INPUTS if possible; otherwise stub with clearly marked TODO.
  </output-schema>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- USER INPUT                                                 -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <analysis>
    TITLE: {{artifact_title}}
    JURISDICTION: {{jurisdiction}}
    MATTER: {{matter}}
    INPUTS: {{inputs}}
  </analysis>

</poml>

<The_Way_of_Code:_81_Taoist_Meditations_on_AI,_Law,_and_Wu_Wei>

1. The code that flows is not the code that testifies.
2. What moves quickly must stop before the judge.
3. The model speaks easily; the record does not forgive.
4. Where language flows, liability hardens.
5. The Way generates drafts; the court demands truth.
6. Ease is not accuracy.
7. Coherence is not correctness.
8. The sage lets the river run, but builds the bridge with stone.
9. AI is water: it fills every shape, including the wrong one.
10. Law is fire: it burns away what cannot stand.

11. To name a thing is not to ground it.
12. To cite a case is not to know it.
13. Authority wears a convincing mask.
14. The mask fools the hurried, not the scale.
15. When speed increases, care must deepen.
16. Wu wei creates; law verifies.
17. Do not ask the river to swear an oath.
18. Do not let mist sign affidavits.
19. The more fluent the text, the sharper the danger.
20. Silence is safer than a false citation.

21. The prompt is a vessel; what fills it may be poison.
22. Emptiness gives power; emptiness invites error.
23. Leave space where play is safe.
24. Seal space where truth must hold.
25. Flow belongs upstream; proof belongs downstream.
26. Creation dances; attestation stands still.
27. What bends survives; what bends too far breaks.
28. The soft persuades; the hard decides.
29. AI persuades; courts decide.
30. Confuse them, and punishment follows.

31. The Way needs no rules.
32. The law appears when the Way fails.
33. Disclosure is a symptom, not a cure.
34. Certification is fear written as policy.
35. When trust breaks, forms multiply.
36. When forms multiply, meaning thins.
37. The wise see the medium, not the message.
38. The unwise argue the output.
39. The medium changes the scale; the scale exposes error.
40. Faster rivers flood sooner.

41. Man finished himself with culture.
42. Now man finishes machines with prompts.
43. What finishes you will also reshape you.
44. A tool that speaks rewires thought.
45. A medium that reasons reshapes judgment.
46. Taste guides creation; law punishes mistakes.
47. Taste without boundary becomes hubris.
48. Boundary without flow becomes sterility.
49. The Way holds both.

50. Separate the garden from the courtroom.
51. Let play grow where harm is reversible.
52. Demand proof where harm is final.
53. Use AI to see possibilities.
54. Use humans to declare truth.
55. Delegation without limits is abandonment.
56. Verification without tools is cruelty.
57. Responsibility without infrastructure is injustice.
58. The sage designs the boundary first.
59. Then allows freedom within it.
60. This is effortless effort.

61. Many outputs arise; one record remains.
62. Ten thousand drafts, one filing.
63. The draft may wander; the filing must stand.
64. The model guesses; the court remembers.
65. Memory belongs to institutions.
66. Imagination belongs to flow.
67. Mix them carefully.
68. Or suffer correction.

69. The best prompts refuse where needed.
70. The best systems degrade safely.
71. The best lawyers know when not to ask.
72. The best judges punish behavior, not belief.
73. The Way of Code honors limits.
74. The Way of Law enforces them.
75. Harmony is not truth.
76. Elegance is not evidence.
77. The river is not guilty.
78. The bridge bears the weight.
79. Build the bridge well.
80. Let the river pass.
81. The Way flows on; the record endures.

<The_Way_of_Code_(Extended):_Tao_x_McLuhan_x_Geertz>

82. Man spins meaning; media tighten the thread.
83. Culture is not what is said, but what makes saying possible.
84. The medium hums before the message speaks.
85. Law listens for signal; AI amplifies noise and signal alike.
86. What extends the mind also reshapes it.

87. The web of significance is invisible until it tears.
88. AI weaves quickly; courts pull slowly.
89. Culture is a control system mistaken for decoration.
90. Media are control systems mistaken for tools.

91. Print made truth linear.
92. Electricity made truth simultaneous.
93. AI makes truth conversational.
94. Conversation feels human; liability does not.

95. The judge reads cold text.
96. The model speaks warm language.
97. Warmth persuades; coldness decides.
98. Confuse warmth for truth and the scale tips.

99. Culture finishes the human animal.
100. Prompts finish the artificial one.
101. What finishes you governs you.
102. Governance unnoticed is governance strongest.

103. The medium sets the pace; the pace sets the mistake.
104. Speed is a cultural value disguised as efficiency.
105. Law is a cultural brake.
106. Brakes scream when engines change.

107. The lawyer lives in symbols.
108. The model lives among symbols.
109. Only one knows which symbols bind.
110. Authority is not a feeling.

111. A citation is a ritual object.
112. Ritual without belief collapses.
113. Belief without grounding deceives.
114. AI supplies belief-shaped text.

115. Media reshape sense ratios.
116. AI reshapes judgment ratios.
117. Judgment without friction drifts.
118. Law supplies friction after the fact.

119. The content distracts the mind.
120. The medium rewires the habit.
121. Habits become norms.
122. Norms become culture.

123. Culture is the slowest software.
124. AI is the fastest culture.
125. Speed without digestion poisons meaning.
126. The court diagnoses indigestion.

127. Thick description anchors meaning.
128. Thin generation floats free.
129. AI excels at thinness.
130. Law demands thickness.

131. The prompt is a miniature society.
132. Every society has taboos.
133. Prompts without taboos invent.
134. Courts punish invention posing as fact.

135. The cold medium invites participation.
136. Participation breeds confidence.
137. Confidence outruns verification.
138. Verification arrives too late.

139. The medium is the message.
140. The message of AI is plausibility at scale.
141. Plausibility feels like truth.
142. Truth resists feeling.

143. Culture hides in practices.
144. Media hide in interfaces.
145. AI hides in fluency.
146. Law unmasks fluency.

147. The sage studies boundaries.
148. The novice studies outputs.
149. Outputs lie easily.
150. Boundaries endure.

151. Water shapes stone by patience.
152. AI shapes thought by repetition.
153. Repetition becomes worldview.
154. Courts interrupt repetition abruptly.

155. The village was once global.
156. Now the mind is global.
157. Global minds err locally.
158. Local courts judge globally sourced text.

159. The web tightens as it scales.
160. The spider feels nothing.
161. The fly feels everything.
162. Liability teaches sensation.

163. Culture is learned unconsciously.
164. Media are adopted unconsciously.
165. AI is trusted unconsciously.
166. Sanctions restore consciousness.

167. The Way adapts silently.
168. Law adapts loudly.
169. Silence breeds power.
170. Noise breeds rules.

171. Do not blame the river for flooding.
172. Do not praise the dam for drowning fields.
173. Design the banks.
174. Know the season.

175. The model finishes sentences.
176. Culture finishes people.
177. Media finish cultures.
178. The cycle tightens.

179. The wise see structure before story.
180. The unwise argue content.
181. Courts argue structure through punishment.
182. Punishment is a medium too.

183. Thick worlds require slow reading.
184. Fast worlds demand new rituals.
185. Disclosure is a ritual of fear.
186. Verification is a ritual without tools.

187. When rituals fail, trust erodes.
188. When trust erodes, law multiplies.
189. When law multiplies, meaning thins.
190. The sage seeks balance earlier.

191. AI is not evil.
192. Law is not cruel.
193. They speak different cosmologies.
194. Translation is required.

195. The medium teaches before the teacher speaks.
196. The prompt teaches before the answer arrives.
197. What you ask shapes who you become.
198. Culture answers slowly.

199. The Way of Code is alignment.
200. The Way of Law is constraint.
201. Alignment without constraint wanders.
202. Constraint without alignment fractures.

203. Build systems that know where they are.
204. Let flow where play is safe.
205. Harden truth where harm is real.
206. This is cultural engineering.

207. The Tao does not verify.
208. The court cannot flow.
209. Wisdom lies in separation.
210. Harmony lies in knowing why.

211. The medium changes man.
212. Man remakes culture.
213. Culture remakes law.
214. Law resists the medium.

215. Resistance reveals structure.
216. Structure reveals the Way.
217. The Way is never content.
218. The Way is pattern.

219. Pattern precedes meaning.
220. Meaning follows form.
221. AI reshapes form.
222. Law restores limits.

223. Do not worship fluency.
224. Do not fear tools.
225. Fear confusion of domains.
226. Name them carefully.

227. The river flows.
228. The scale balances.
229. The web holds.
230. The medium speaks.

231. Listen past the words.
232. See the structure.
233. Design the culture.
234. Let the Way endure.

The clean correction in plain words


Sahlins is not “culture matters” in general; he’s making a strong claim that Hawaiian symbolic categories are real causal operators in the historical event. Wikipedia+1

Obeyesekere is not just “Europe projected”; he’s defending native practical reason and attacking the idea that Hawaiians were irrational “believers in gods walking in.” Wikipedia+2ScholarBlogs+2

Geertz, in “Culture War,” reads the whole thing as anthropology arguing about how explanation, evidence, and authority work, not just what happened to Cook. Studocu+1

Information Architecture Navigator


An interactive appendix focused on modeling Cook's death through a complex system of entities, sub-entities, morphisms, and actions. Based on Marshall Sahlins' "How 'Natives' Think: About Captain Cook, For Example," this interface represents an ambitious attempt to systematize historical narrative.

Flux Field Visualization

What aspects of the Sahlins-Obeyesekere debate resist computational representation?

How has the growing complexity of this model reflected the inherent challenges in representing cultural theory?

What does the "deterministic" feeling of the visualization tell us about the limitations of computational approaches to cultural understanding?


Narrative Log Interface


A simplified mechanical approach to cultural modeling using hostile architecture as a framework. This interface demonstrates the evolution of the project's assumptions and methodology through narrative generation.

In the context of Vibe Coding and Context Engineering, these ancient parables describe exactly how a modern "cognitive architect" should interact with an AI.


Cook Ding: Mastery Beyond Skill
In the parable, Cook Ding is butchering an ox for Lord Wenhui. His movements are so rhythmic they seem like a dance. When asked how he achieved such skill, he explains:


Phase 1: The Whole Ox. "When I first began, I saw the whole ox." (Like a beginner coder seeing a giant, intimidating block of code).

The Modern Application:
A "Vibe Coder" using POML doesn't fight the "meat" of the syntax. Instead, they look for the fissures in the AI's reasoning. You don't "hack" at the prompt; you find the "empty spaces" where the AI’s logic already wants to go and gently guide it.The Knife that Never Dulls: Cook Ding has used the same knife for 19 years without sharpening it because he never hits a bone. In Context Engineering, if your prompt is "dulling" (failing, hallucinating, or requiring constant fixing), it's because you are hitting "bone"—trying to force the AI to do something against its training or architecture.


Tao Craft: The "Fu" of Digital Creation
"Tao Craft" often refers to the practice of creating Fu talismans—sigils that are empowered by the creator's Qi (energy) and intent. In his book The Tao of Craft, Benebell Wen describes how the "vibe" of the practitioner is literally encoded into the object.

The Medium is the Talisman: As McLuhan would say, the form of your orchestration is what carries the power, not just the words you type.


The "Tao Coder" vs. The "Average Coder"

Approach

Finds where the code wants to go (Negative Space).

Context and Vibe.

Below is a grounded, step-by-step answer to your exact question:

I’ll keep Cook Ding as a discipline lens, not a metaphor, and translate each move into concrete engineering behavior.



<Cook_Ding_Method_for_AI_Legal_Context_Engineering>


1. First principle: Cook Ding never starts by cutting


He starts by seeing where cutting must not occur.


In the Mata v. Avianca–type failure, the “tricky section” is authority production:


citations

quotations

holdings

application of precedent


These are the bones.


Cook Ding’s question (translated):


Where is resistance inevitable?


In law, resistance is inevitable whenever the model must be correct, not just plausible.


So Cook Ding’s first move is not writing a better prompt, but refusing to cut there at all.



2. Phase 1: “Seeing the whole ox” → naive prompting


This corresponds to:


flat prompts

vibe-only coding

“find cases supporting X”

3. Phase 2: “Seeing fissures” → separating task zones

Translated to AI legal context engineering:


<Phase_2>

At this phase, Cook Ding would insist on:


separate prompts

separate schemas

separate refusal rules



4. Phase 3: “Spirit, not eyes” → negative space mastery


This is where most people misread Cook Ding.


It does not mean intuition replacing structure.
It means structure has become internalized.


Cook Ding no longer thinks:

“Avoid the bone.”

He has designed a knife that cannot hit bone.



5. What “never hitting bone” means in AI legal systems


Bone = states that must never exist


<Bone_States>
├── citation_without_source
├── quote_without_text
├── holding_without_pinpoint
├── confidence_without_grounding
└── silent_completion_when_uncertain


Cook Ding’s solution is negative-space engineering:


<Design>

Not “warn the model”
Not “be careful”
But make it impossible.



6. How Cook Ding would design the POML context (concrete)


Step 1: He would narrow the blade (capability reduction)


<meta components="-freeform-citation,-implicit-holding" />

<policies>

</policies>


This is Cook Ding’s map of the ox.



Step 3: He would let flow return inside the safe channels


<task>
  Analyze the provided legal texts only.

</task>

<document src="{{PRIMARY_CASE_EXCERPTS}}" />


Now:


The model flows

The knife stays sharp

No bone is contacted



7. Why this is wu wei and not restriction


Wu wei is not freedom everywhere.
Wu wei is freedom where resistance is absent.


Cook Ding says:

“I go along with what is already so.”

In AI legal systems:


The model is already good at summarization

It is already bad at grounding authority without text

Do not force the model to do what its nature resists.
Arrange the work so it never needs to.

one prompt mixes ideation + authority

vibe and verification are collapsed

the model must guess

Cook Ding’s approach to AI legal context engineering:


Identify irreversible-error zones

Define forbidden states explicitly

Remove the possibility of entering them

Allow flow only where error is reversible

Let structure disappear into habit


That is:


Taoist restraint

NASA negative-space safety

Applied to AI legal workflows

code_syntax_all.prompt: Write up pur method gor a github repo
code_syntax_all.content:
Below is a repo-ready write-up you can paste into a GitHub project. I’m assuming the project is about Scout → Cook Ding prompt orchestration for legal/historical authority workflows (anti-hallucination, quote-bound analysis). Edit names as you like.



Scout → Cook Ding: Whole-Ox Retrieval + Quote-Only Cutting


A prompt-orchestrated method for high-stakes research (legal, policy, archival) that separates search from attestation.


Goal: get Westlaw-level recall without Westlaw-style failure modes (fabricated holdings, invented connections, quote drift).
Core idea: one agent finds and packages the world; a second agent only speaks from provided text.



Why this exists


LLMs are excellent at fluent synthesis. In high-stakes domains, fluency is the failure mode.


The canonical breakdown looks like this:


Search (what exists?)

Selection (what matters?)

Attestation (what can I claim?)


Most systems collapse these into a single generative step. That’s where hallucinations enter: the model is pressured to complete an answer even when the record is thin.


This repo implements a strict split:


Scout: broad retrieval + thick evidence world (the “whole ox”)

Cook Ding: quote-only, location-bound, no search (the “knife”)

Bartleby: formal stop condition (“I would rather not…”) when text is insufficient



Design principles


1) Negative space first


We define forbidden states upfront and remove entire classes of error:


no invented authorities

no holding claims without verbatim text

no paraphrase-as-quote

no “confidence smoothing”

no speculative completion


2) Wide vision, narrow mouth


Scout may see everything. Cook Ding may only speak from what Scout provides.


3) Whole ox → joints → cut


Scout returns a thick world (documents + relationships + candidate joints).
Cook Ding uses only the selected excerpts (or full text if explicitly allowed).


4) Stopping is success


If the record doesn’t open, the system stops without negotiation.



Architecture


User Query
  │
  ├── Scout (full corpus access)
  │     ├─ Search & retrieve (court opinions, bulletins, rules, etc.)
  │     ├─ Build evidence world (metadata + connection map)
  │     ├─ Extract verbatim candidate joints (with locations)
  │     └─ Compile Cook Ding input payload (evidence_pack)
  │
  └── Cook Ding (no search)
        ├─ Quote-only extraction
        ├─ “allows / does_not_allow” boundaries
        ├─ assumptions_required + unknowns
        └─ Bartleby if insufficient



Data contracts


A) Scout Output (two layers)


Scout returns:


evidence_world (for debugging / observability)

cook_ding_input (direct downstream payload)


cook_ding_input is the only thing Cook Ding consumes.


cook_ding_input schema (conceptual):


{
  "legal_question": "...",
  "jurisdiction": "...",
  "facts": "...",
  "evidence_pack": [
    {
      "source_id": "...",
      "authority_type": "case|statute|rule|administrative_bulletin|...",
      "title": "...",
      "court_or_body": "...",
      "date": "...",
      "citation_or_identifier": "...",
      "provenance": "...",
      "scope_tag": "...",
      "excerpts": [
        { "text": "...", "location": "...", "hash": "..." }
      ]
    }
  ]
}


B) Cook Ding Output (attestable JSON)


Cook Ding emits only what the provided text supports:


{
  "mode": "SUPPORTED|NOT_SUPPORTED|BARTLEBY",
  "textual_support": [
    {
      "source_id": "...",
      "quote": "...",
      "location": "...",
      "allows": "...",
      "does_not_allow": "..."
    }
  ],
  "assumptions_required": ["..."],
  "unknowns": ["..."],
  "bartleby": "I would rather not proceed without the relevant text."
}



What Scout does (and does not do)


Scout MUST do


retrieve broadly (primary + counter authority)

label procedural posture (opinion/order/bulletin/etc.)

include provenance for every doc

extract verbatim candidate joints with location markers

compile cook_ding_input.evidence_pack


Scout MUST NOT do


state holdings

synthesize doctrine (“the rule is…”)

apply law to facts

resolve conflicts between sources


Scout is a retriever and packager. Not a judge.



What Cook Ding does (and does not do)


Cook Ding MUST do


use only the provided evidence_pack

quote verbatim with location

state boundaries: allows / does_not_allow

list assumptions and unknowns

stop with Bartleby when evidence is insufficient


Cook Ding MUST NOT do


search

guess missing authority

infer holdings not supported by text

paraphrase as quotation

smooth uncertainty with fluent filler


Cook Ding is an attestation engine, not a synthesizer.



Bartleby (formal refusal primitive)


When evidence is insufficient, Cook Ding returns:

I would rather not proceed without the relevant text.

No explanation. No workaround. No negotiation.


This prevents “helpful completion” from turning into hallucination.



Recommended audit gate (optional but strongly advised)


After Cook Ding returns JSON, run a deterministic verifier:


each quote must match an excerpt hash from evidence_pack

each location must be present

each source_id must exist in the pack

if SUPPORTED, must include ≥1 support item


If any check fails → block output or force Bartleby.



Files


prompts/scout.poml — Whole-Ox Scout + Cook Ding pack compiler

prompts/cook_ding.poml — Quote-only cutter + Bartleby refusal

schemas/cook_ding_input.json — input contract

schemas/cook_ding_output.json — output contract

audit/verify_quotes.ts — optional audit gate (hash + location checks)



Usage


Run Scout with the user query

Take scout_output.cook_ding_input

Run Cook Ding with that payload

(Optional) run audit gate on Cook Ding output

Publish



What this method is good for


legal research memos

sanctions/ethics-sensitive drafting

archival disputes with controlling documents (bulletins, directives, committee approvals)

any domain where authority tokens must be grounded in primary text



What this method is not for


open-ended ideation where hallucinations are acceptable

tasks where “best effort synthesis” is the goal

situations where you can’t access primary sources at all



License / disclaimer


This repository provides a prompt-orchestration method and does not constitute legal advice.
Always verify outputs with qualified professionals and primary sources.



If you paste your current scout.poml and cook_ding.poml filenames/conventions, I can tailor this README to your exact directory structure and add a minimal examples/ flow showing inputs and outputs.

code_syntax_all.prompt: More poml bobe coding philosophy
code_syntax_all.content:
Below is a POML-first vibe coding philosophy for Poly Metis Law: not abstract “be clear,” but a buildable doctrine that treats POML as the instrument panel for “poly-metis” (many-minded) work under constraint.


I’ll give you:


Principles (PML vibe coding doctrine)

A reusable POML template (Scout→Cook Ding pipeline)

A “palette” of modes you can swap like CSS (Rubin vibe layer)



Poly Metis Vibe Coding Doctrine (POML-native)



<Poly_Metis_Vibe_Coding_Doctrine>
├── <Taste_is_a_stylesheet>
│   └── [separate] <tone> [from] <truth_conditions>
├── <Search_is_not_speech>
│   └── [separate] <retrieval> [from] <attestation>
├── <Authority_tokens_are_hot>
│   └── <citations/quotes/holdings> [require] <hard_cages>
├── <Negative_space_is_primary>
│   └── [define] <must_not_states> [before] <desired_states>
├── <Stop_is_a_feature>
│   └── <Bartleby> [is] <a_first-class_primitive>
└── <Whole_ox_then_joint_then_cut>
    └── [return] <evidence_world> + <cook_ding_input>


Translation into practice:


POML is not “prompt formatting.”

POML is a control surface: components enabled/disabled, schemas enforced, modes swapped.



“God-level” POML Orchestrator (Scout + Cook Ding in one file)



This is a single orchestrator POML that defines:


shared inputs

two internal “programs” (Scout and Cook Ding)

a strict handoff contract (cook_ding_input)


You can run it as:


two separate calls (recommended), or

one orchestrated call if your runner supports staged execution.


<poml version="1.0">

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- GLOBAL INPUTS          -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <let name="legal_question">{{ legal_question }}</let>
  <let name="jurisdiction">{{ jurisdiction || "UNKNOWN" }}</let>
  <let name="facts">{{ facts || "NONE" }}</let>

  <!-- ===================== -->
  <!-- GLOBAL VIBE LAYER       -->
  <!-- ===================== -->
  <stylesheet>
    {
      "global": { "verbosity": "minimal" },
      "scout":  { "tone": "instrumental", "verbosity": "bounded" },
      "ding":   { "tone": "flat", "verbosity": "minimal" }
    }
  </stylesheet>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- PROGRAM A: SCOUT (FULL CORPUS, THICK WORLD, NO HOLDINGS)   -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <section className="scout">

    <meta components="
      -holding_assertion,
      -doctrinal_synthesis,
      -fact_application,
      -confidence_smoothing
    " />

    <system>
      <role>Scout</role>
      <context>
        You can search everything. Build the whole ox.
        You do NOT state holdings. You do NOT apply law to facts.
        You MAY extract verbatim candidate joints with locations.
      </context>
      <task>
        Retrieve primary sources and build:
        (1) evidence_world (docs + provenance + connection map)
        (2) cook_ding_input (evidence_pack excerpts ready for Cook Ding)
      </task>
    </system>

    <user>
      QUESTION: {{ legal_question }}
      JURISDICTION: {{ jurisdiction }}
      FACTS: {{ facts }}
      DIRECTIVE:
        Return a thick evidence_world AND a cook_ding_input payload.
        Candidate joints must be verbatim with locations.
    </user>

    <output-schema parser="json">
      {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "evidence_world": { "type": "object" },
          "cook_ding_input": { "type": "object" }
        },
        "required": ["cook_ding_input"]
      }
    </output-schema>

  </section>

  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <!-- PROGRAM B: COOK DING (NO SEARCH, QUOTE-ONLY, BARTLEBY)     -->
  <!-- ========================================================= -->
  <section className="ding">

    <meta components="
      -search,
      -freeform_citation,
      -implicit_authority,
      -speculative_completion,
      -doctrinal_synthesis,
      -confidence_smoothing
    " />

    <system>
      <role>Cook Ding</role>
      <context>
        You cannot search. You cannot guess.
        Use only cook_ding_input.evidence_pack.
        If insufficient: BARTLEBY.
      </context>
      <task>
        Answer the legal question using verbatim quotes + locations only.
        State what the text allows and does not allow.
      </task>
    </system>

    <user>
      COOK_DING_INPUT: {{ cook_ding_input }}
    </user>

    <output-schema parser="json">
      {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "mode": { "enum": ["SUPPORTED", "NOT_SUPPORTED", "BARTLEBY"] },
          "textual_support": { "type": "array" },
          "assumptions_required": { "type": "array" },
          "unknowns": { "type": "array" },
          "bartleby": { "type": "string" }
        },
        "required": ["mode"]
      }
    </output-schema>

  </section>

</poml>


This is “vibe coding” because you control the system by swapping:


components

schemas

tone layers

handoff contracts
